title: Partial Payments and the PracticePay Late Fee
content:
A late fee on a PracticePay Patient Financing plan is scaled by what was paid toward the due date it is charged for.

**Rule.** The partial-payment share of a late fee looks at the latest payment entry credited toward that due date, the one recorded first where two share the latest date: when that payment has not come back as a returned payment and is dated no later than the last day of the grace period, the share is the unpaid part divided by the monthly payment amount; when it has not come back and is dated after the last day of the grace period, the share is the unpaid part divided by the monthly payment amount but never less than 0.5; when it has come back, or no payment entry was credited toward that due date, the share is 1. The grace period's last day is the monthly due date plus the plan's late-fee grace days in calendar days, counted from the day after the due date.

The unpaid part is the smaller of the monthly payment amount and the amount past due less open disputed amounts, never below zero.

## Three ways of working the share

| Latest payment credited toward the due date | Share |
|---|---|
| not come back, dated on or before the grace period's last day | unpaid part divided by the monthly payment amount |
| not come back, dated after the grace period's last day | the same ratio, but never less than 0.5 |
| came back, or none credited | 1 |

## Worked figures (hypothetical monthly payment 200.00, unpaid part 70.00, due date 1 May, 10-day grace period ending 11 May)

- Partial payment dated 9 May: share 70.00 divided by 200.00, that is 0.35.
- Partial payment dated 15 May: the ratio 0.35 is below 0.5, so the share is 0.5.
- Payment dated 9 May that came back: share 1.
